value.loc: Abstract p.230; Sec. 4 p.233; Sec. 5.2 p.235; Sec. 6 p.235
value.quote: study the obtained runoff rules from an axiomatic point of view
value.note: SB from weak strategyproofness (Theorem 1), since the codebook counts strategyproofness as a property under SB; SI from Gaussian simulations; EM from French election and poster datasets.

C1.reason: Theorem 1 is a main result on strategyproofness, which the SB definition explicitly includes as a property.

value.quote: voters are strategic and cast insincere approval ballots
value.note: Footnote 4 and the deviation analysis treat submitted ballots as possibly differing from held preferences. The main text also assumes sincere ballots, citing convention, so IDJ could fit; DIST is listed first.

C2.4.reason: Footnote 4 says submitted ballots may differ from held preferences, which meets DIST, and IDS is wrong because a convention-type reason is given.

value.quote: discount the satisfaction of voters who are already satisfied
value.note: Satisfaction is tied informally to approved finalists; no utility notion is defined.

C4.1.reason: The paper's own Section 3.2 uses voter satisfaction, so C4.1 applies, and its relation to approvals is only mentioned informally, not defined.

value.quote: we concentrate on the counting of sincere ballots cast by a fixed electorate
value.note: The needed assumption is that ballots reflect held preferences and that the electorate is fixed; the paper states it in Section 1, including the exclusion of between-round dynamics.

C9.2.reason: The needed sincerity and fixed-electorate assumptions are stated in Section 1, and the codebook does not require them to be restated in the conclusion.
